title: Nasdaq 100 sinks 6% as chipmaker selloff deepens
article:
(Nov 6): A post-election slide in chipmakers snowballed, dragging the Nasdaq 100 down 6%, as investors bailed from the sector on speculation the Democratic sweep in Congress will usher in a new era of regulation for the artificial-intelligence (AI) industry.

The 11% plunge in a gauge of chip giants put the group on track for its worst week since the April 2025 tariff meltdown. Nvidia Corp slid 8%. Qualcomm Inc and Arm Holdings plc’s sank on underwhelming outlooks. Apple Inc plans to raise about US$7 billion from an investment-grade bond sale, adding to a flurry of tech issuance. Tesla Inc and SpaceX each lost 11%. Bitcoin fell 5.5%.

“The rotation out of chipmakers reflects growing concern about the pace and funding of AI spending due to the risk of more regulations after the blue wave, even as earnings remain resilient and valuations have reset sharply,” said Chris Murphy at Susquehanna International Group.

In a rush for safety, defensive industries like consumer staples and healthcare climbed. The swoon in tech shares also lifted bonds despite a rebound in oil prices. Haven currencies including the yen and the Swiss franc outperformed.

The AI trade is here to stay, but it remains volatile, and investors should not overlook some of the more boring areas of the market, according to Bob Edwards at Edwards Asset Management.

See also: Nasdaq 100 sinks 5% as chipmaker sell-off deepens

“We are not concerned about what the blue wave means for the buildout of AI, since the president still has the veto pen and data centres bring jobs and tax revenue,” he said.

Data centres have become an easy political target amid rising electricity bills. Bipartisan energy permitting reform could help by accelerating new power generation and transmission, while politicians will aim to ensure developers pay for the incremental grid infrastructure required to serve them, according to Jordan Jackson and Stephanie Aliaga at JPMorgan Asset Management.

The elections reinforced growing opposition to data centers, particularly in Texas and Ohio, where incoming Democratic governors favour tougher development conditions, they said. However, despite the backlash, statewide moratoriums have struggled to become law, accorrding to the strategists

See also: Krispy Kreme raises revenue outlook as turnaround takes hold

“Politicians may now feel emboldened to adopt a harder stance but face competing pressures to protect ratepayers while attracting jobs, investment and tax revenues. AI remains an evolving public issue and is not yet a clear voter priority,” they noted.
• Microsoft Corp, one of Nscale’s primary customers, opted not to extend a contract at a Texas data centre with the startup ahead of its planned public offering, according to a person familiar with the matter.
• Micron Technology Inc has suspended plans for a memory chip plant in Taiwan due to a protracted labour dispute, according to people familiar with the matter, throwing into question the fate of a major production base for crucial AI components.
• Amazon.com Inc is adding Uber Technologies Inc restaurant delivery perks on its shopping site for Prime members, forging a deeper partnership just a week after rival service DoorDash Inc agreed to acquire Instacart.
• Peloton Interactive Inc forecast holiday-quarter revenue that was slightly above Wall Street’s expectations, even as the fitness company projected a year-over-year sales decline and narrower profit margins.
• Wendy’s Co board unanimously rejected an offer from a group led by Nelson Peltz’s Trian Fund Management to buy out the burger chain for about US$1.4 billion, saying the proposal substantially undervalues the company’s prospects and long-term earnings potential.

Conlay by E&O brings luxury urban resort living skywards in Kuala Lumpur
article:
With its crisp, white fins and dramatic picture-frame openings, Conlay by E&O has become one of the most distinctive towers on the Kuala Lumpur skyline.

Rising 51 storeys at the junction of the Jalan Kia Peng and Jalan Conlay streets, the 491-unit freehold serviced apartment development was completed in the second quarter of 2025.

The design is a collaboration between Kuala Lumpur-based architectural and design firm GDP Architects, and Kerry Hill Architects, a firm known for crafting spaces deeply responsive to climate, culture and place.

The project, which pairs residential living with hotel-style service, was the Top Development (Central Malaysia) winner in the high-rise category at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026.

Conlay by E&O is developed by a joint venture between Malaysia-listed Eastern & Oriental Berhad (E&O) and Japan's Mitsui Fudosan Group.

Of the 491 units at the luxury project, 297 are fully furnished residences on Levels 12 to 33A, in one-bedroom to two-bedroom-plus-study layouts ranging from 743 to 1,335 sq ft. The remaining 194 units, on Levels 37 to 51, form the branded residence component.

Launched in 2019 with prices from RM1.8 million, the residences drew strong interest from foreign buyers, particularly those from Taiwan, Hong Kong, mainland China and South Korea.

On the EdgeProp.my portal, a one-bedroom serviced apartment at the development currently commands a monthly rent of between RM5,000 and RM7,000 (about $1,560 to $2,190).

Open-plan living with understated luxury

Conceived as an urban resort, the tower’s fin-lined facade gives it a strong architectural identity. The fins also act as passive shading devices, cutting solar heat gain and keeping interiors comfortable in the tropical climate.

The large picture-frame openings, meanwhile, enable sweeping views of Plaza Conlay, the Tun Razak Exchange and the Royal Selangor Golf Club in central Kuala Lumpur.

Inside the development, open-plan living areas and full-height glazing draw in natural light and maximise the views.

The interiors, by E&O’s in-house team, follow a philosophy of understated luxury, with a palette of timber, stone, marble and leather softened by warm lighting. Kitchens come fully fitted with premium appliances, and materials were chosen for their durability and ease of maintenance as much as for their looks.

Hotel service at home

What sets Conlay by E&O apart is its service-led approach. Drawing on the hospitality heritage of the group behind the iconic Eastern & Oriental Hotel in Penang, the development offers residents five-star services through a dedicated concierge, supported by a digital community platform, upon request for the Signature Suites.

The aim is to combine the privacy of homeownership with the personalised attention usually found in a premium hotel.

That hospitality extends to the arrival experience, with dedicated residential lobbies, and to a generous suite of communal spaces.

Residents have access to a library, music room, billiard room, multimedia room, meeting room and multi-purpose lounge, along with fitness centres, saunas and jacuzzis. On Level 50, a lifestyle and dining destination pairs culinary experiences with sky-high city views.

Greener by design

Three signature sky gardens bring greenery and communal space into the vertical environment, offering residents places to relax, exercise and socialise above the city.

The landscape design by Seksan Design complements the tower’s contemporary tropical architecture.

Among the highlights is the heated infinity pool set within one of the tower’s framed openings, against a backdrop of the Kuala Lumpur skyline. Outdoor decks and lounges extend the resort atmosphere.

Together, the greenery, open spaces and panoramic views support residents' physical and mental well-being while fostering a sense of community.

Conlay by E&O has been awarded GreenRE Gold provisional certification by Malaysia’s Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association.

Low-emissivity glass helps keep the heat out, while energy-efficient lifts, LED lighting and ceiling fans reduce power use. The elevated car parks are naturally ventilated.

Harvested rainwater irrigates the gardens, while sub-metering of major water uses helps catch leaks early. Recycling bins on every residential floor make it easy for residents to sort their waste.

Green cement, low-VOC paints that reduce the emission of toxic fumes, and certified sustainable building products were used in construction.

Residents can access the Conlay MRT Station, on the Putrajaya Line, at the development’s doorstep, as well as electric-vehicle charging points and bicycle parking.

Given its timeless architecture, hotel-grade service and resort-style amenities, Conlay by E&O sets a new benchmark for luxury high-rise living in Kuala Lumpur.

title: Bon Kiara: Spacious, garden-centred living in Kuala Lumpur's Mont Kiara
article:
Mont Kiara, an affluent township northwest of downtown Kuala Lumpur, is known for its dense cluster of high-rise condos, but Bon Kiara by Malaysian boutique property developer Bon Estates has set out to offer something different.

The 410-unit freehold development on Jalan Kiara 3 in Mont Kiara features homes of 2,081 to 3,075 sq ft, with just six units per floor, set around 1.5 acres (0.61ha) of landscaped green space.

The project, which is under construction, won the Top Development (Central Malaysia) title in the high-rise category at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026.

Bon Kiara, the second project by Bon Estates, sits on a 4.15-acre (1.68ha) site. It comprises 64 three-bedroom units, 204 four-bedroom units, and 142 units with five bedrooms or more.

With the first sale and purchase agreement signed in March 2023, the development is slated for completion and handover by late 2026.

Positioned at an accessible luxury price point averaging RM700 (about $218) psf, the homes cater to multi-generational families, growing families who need more room, and older homeowners downsizing from landed properties. The project has drawn mainly owner-occupiers, with Malaysians making up about 70% of buyers, and foreign buyers and investors the remaining 30%.

“Buyers are not simply looking for more square footage. They are looking for homes that better support the way they want to live,” says Bon Estates’ CEO Chan Jin-Wy.

Contemporary Mediterranean resort style

Designed by JS Lim Architect under a “Cosmosphere” concept inspired by the cosmos flower, Bon Kiara adopts a contemporary Mediterranean resort style, with warm earth tones, clean lines and layered facades.

The massing is modulated to reduce visual bulk, while landscaping on the podium and sky levels softens the built form. Inside, column-free layouts give owners the flexibility to arrange their homes as their needs change, while clear zoning keeps living and resting areas private.

Interiors by SSO Studio feature warm neutrals and natural textures, including solid wood flooring certified by the Forest Stewardship Council.

Each unit has a semi-open lanai — a covered, versatile indoor-outdoor hybrid room — in place of a typical balcony, with sliding glass doors to buffer the heat and draw in natural breezes.

A ‘padang’ in the city

“Rather than maximising built-up space at the expense of greenery, we dedicated approximately 1.5 acres (0.61ha) to green and open spaces,” says Chan. “Our vision was to demonstrate that vertical living does not have to mean sacrificing space, greenery or a sense of home.”

Designed by PAD Space Artisan, the central park re-creates the open padang, or field, usually found in landed neighbourhoods. Part of it sits above the development’s on-site detention tank, turning utility space into usable greenery.

A network of paths links the jogging trails, swimming pool, pickleball court, yoga deck and 2,000 sq ft gym, while a Social House, co-working spaces and a Kids’ Lounge encourage neighbours to mingle. Pets have their own park too.

Location is another draw, with Gardens International School, grocers and eateries within walking distance.

The developer has also looked beyond its own boundaries. To ease traffic along Jalan Kiara 3, Bon Estates has built a connecting road towards the Jalan Duta Kiara street and Solaris Dutamas mixed-used project as a corporate social responsibility initiative.

“A good residential development should be considered not only by what is within its boundaries, but also by how it connects to the surrounding neighbourhood,” says Chan.

Bon Kiara has achieved GreenRE Gold certification, with low-emissivity glass on east- and west-facing units keeping interiors cool, while energy-efficient air-conditioners and common-area services are expected to cut carbon emissions by about 1,433 tonnes a year.

Solar energy powers the common areas, and harvested rainwater irrigates the gardens. Every unit comes with an electric-vehicle charger isolator and a designated parking bay, and a residents’ shuttle makes it easy to get around.

What’s next for the developer

Bon Estates is now developing Yanu Hills in Taman Melawati, its first landed project in the Klang Valley, comprising 10 luxury bungalows. It is also planning a third high-rise development in central Kuala Lumpur.

Beyond Malaysia’s borders, the developer sees as potential buyers Malaysians working in Singapore who are considering a home in the Klang Valley, as well as Singaporeans familiar with Kuala Lumpur’s property market.

“Our approach is to focus on buyers whose needs align with our product offering, rather than pursuing overseas markets simply for the sake of expansion,” says Chan.

title: Nasdaq 100 sinks 5% as chipmaker sell-off deepens
article:
(Nov 5): The rout in chipmakers gathered pace, with investors weighing any potential impacts of a Democratic sweep of Congress on the artificial intelligence (AI) trade that has powered the bull market in stocks.

A gauge of chip giants extended a plunge from a June record to 36%. Nvidia Corp slid 7.9%. Qualcomm Inc and Arm Holdings plc also sank on underwhelming outlooks. The Nasdaq 100 lost 5%. Apple Inc plans to raise about US$7 billion ($8.9 billion) from an investment-grade bond sale, adding to a flurry of issuance. Tesla Inc and SpaceX each slumped about 10%. Bitcoin fell 5%.

“The rotation out of chipmakers reflects growing concern about the pace and funding of AI spending due to the risk of more regulations after the blue wave, even as earnings remain resilient and valuations have reset sharply,” said Chris Murphy at Susquehanna International Group.

In a rush for safety, defensive industries like consumer staples and health care climbed. Treasuries rose, with traders also gearing up for the jobs report. Haven currencies including the yen and the Swiss franc outperformed.

The AI trade is here to stay, but it remains volatile, and investors should not overlook some of the more boring areas of the market, according to Bob Edwards at Edwards Asset Management.

“We are not concerned about what the blue wave means for the buildout of AI, since the president still has the veto pen and data centres bring jobs and tax revenue,” he said.

See also: Krispy Kreme raises revenue outlook as turnaround takes hold

“Stay invested in diversified equities,” said Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi at UBS Global Wealth Management. “Strong earnings, resilient economic growth, and robust demand for AI infrastructure continue to support our constructive view.”

It’s worth remembering that demand for data centres is such that the AI infrastructure companies have long found themselves struggling to keep up with demand, according to Kent Fung at Fundstrat Global Advisors.

“Remember when nervous investors worried about Nvidia’s inability, for various reasons, to sell advanced chips to Chinese customers? It turned out that demand had so far outstripped Nvidia’s production capacity that it didn’t matter anyway,” he said.

title: Apple seeks about US$7 bil from first bond sale in over a year — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 5): Apple Inc is planning to raise about US$7 billion ($8.9 billion) from its first investment-grade bond offering in more than a year to help fund share buybacks, adding to a flurry of debt issuance by US technology heavyweights.

No final decision has been made on the size of the sale, which may still change depending on investor demand, according to people familiar with the matter. Proceeds from the offering are set to be used for general corporate purposes, including stock buybacks, dividends and capital expenditures, the people said.

The iPhone maker is selling debt in seven tranches, with maturities ranging from two to 10 years, the people added, asking not to be identified because they’re not authorised to speak publicly. Initial price talk on the longest tenor is a spread of 0.8 percentage point over Treasuries, the person added.

“Apple’s return to the bond market appears more opportunistic than funding-driven, raising proceeds available for buybacks and dividends,” said Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Robert Schiffman. For Apple, “shareholder returns remain a greater capital priority than the massive AI infrastructure spending confronting hyperscaler peers”.

The move follows a flurry of Big Tech debt issuance, with Microsoft Corp, Oracle Corp and Meta Platforms Inc raising a combined US$50 billion in the US market since last week as part of efforts to fund their investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Those deals have come with juicier yields, as investors demand added compensation amid growing scepticism about whether the AI-focused spending spree will pay off.

See also: Goldman, Apollo in talks to sell SpaceX’s US$40 bil AI deal — Bloomberg

Apple last sold bonds in May 2025, when it raised US$4.5 billion.

Bank of America Corp, Deutsche Bank AG, Goldman Sachs Group Inc and JPMorgan Chase & Co are managing the transaction, the people added.

title: Goldman, Apollo in talks to sell SpaceX’s US$40 bil AI deal — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 5): Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Apollo Global Management Inc are in talks with Wall Street investors to start selling portions of a roughly US$40 billion chip financing deal for SpaceX, just as the artificial intelligence (AI) boom braces for upheaval following a sweeping Democratic victory.

The two firms have begun approaching potential buyers for the multi-tranche financing, according to people familiar with the matter. The deal, structured to keep the debt off SpaceX’s balance sheet, is the largest arrangement of its kind for graphics processing units (GPUs) on record, SpaceX has said.

In some cases, investors are being asked to purchase slices of as much as US$500 million before the official syndication process starts, in an effort to swiftly close the transaction, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing private information. Syndication is slated to start soon, according to the people.

Representatives for Apollo and Goldman declined to comment. A representative for SpaceX didn’t respond to a request for comment.

Elon Musk’s rocket, satellite and AI venture announced the financing in October, with investors agreeing to the package before it priced.

See also: Claude lowers ChatGPT’s lead in US$1.4 bil UK consumer AI market

That exposed lenders to market risk during a volatile period. Investors have retreated from the AI trade, questioning whether revenues can ever justify the breathtaking spend — a sentiment that turned lenders against some of SpaceX’s neocloud competitors, including CoreWeave Inc.

Those pressures intensified after the Democrats swept into power in Congress following midterm elections, riding a wave of voter concerns over higher living costs and the war in Iran. Data centres too became a fierce electoral flashpoint, particularly in Texas, which flipped blue just months after freezing new project approvals.

As the political landscape shifted overnight, the market reacted sharply, sending shares of both SpaceX and Tesla Inc lower. SpaceX’s data centres are based in Memphis, Tennessee, and it’s developing other sites in Mississippi.

See also: Meta gets record €53 bil of orders for debut euro bonds

Under the US$40 billion deal — a win for Musk — a special purpose vehicle managed by Apollo-backed Atlas SP will buy Nvidia Corp chips and issue the debt held by lenders, Bloomberg previously reported. By using this structure, SpaceX protects its corporate credit ratings.

SpaceX will rent the chips through a five-year agreement, according to a presentation seen by Bloomberg News, but is not providing a residual value guarantee or other commitments that have become common for tech firms to secure financing. “SpaceX’s obligation to pay rent is absolute,” according to the presentation.

Crucially, the documents show SpaceX cannot use force majeure clauses to pause its payments — a contrast to firms like Oracle Corp, which Bloomberg previously reported has cited force majeure in an attempt to put off its data centre obligations.

“Rent is owed regardless of equipment condition, casualty or force majeure, providing investors with a clean look-through to SpaceX credit,” the document said.

The debt is structured in several tranches, including an US$8.3 billion senior-secured loan that will be syndicated to the banks, and several tranches of bonds that will be sold to asset managers, according to the people. Goldman led the loan portion, while Apollo was the key investor in the bonds, the people said. Pacific Investment Management Co also participated in the deal.

The debt package, along with a lease prepayment of US$7 billion, will be used to pay for about US$47.3 billion of GPU equipment, namely Nvidia’s latest Rubin chips, the documents showed. The chips will be delivered in the first half of 2027.

A gauge of SpaceX credit risk jumped in early trading on Thursday. Credit-default swaps used to protect against losses on the company’s debt increased about 12 basis points (bps) to 282bps, according to ICE Data Services, near a record 284bps reached on Friday. The price of those contracts has surged from 150bps during the past two months as investors grew increasingly concerned about the level of debt being taken on to fund the AI buildout.

title: US labour productivity increases at fastest pace in a year
article:
(Nov 5): US labour productivity accelerated in the third quarter (3Q) at the fastest pace in a year, suggesting a capital spending boom is translating into greater efficiency at a time when input costs have soared.

Productivity, or non-farm business output per hour, increased at a 3.6% annualised rate after an upwardly revised 2.1% pace in the prior quarter, data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics showed on Thursday.

Unit labour costs — what businesses pay employees to produce one unit of output — fell 0.7%, the first decline since the second quarter of 2025.

Labour costs are the biggest expense for many businesses, so companies invest in new technology and equipment to allow their workers to become more efficient. Productivity growth can help firms limit price hikes for consumers and other businesses.

Companies have poured massive amounts of money into artificial intelligence (AI), software and equipment — investment that businesses anticipate will allow them to generate more output with the same amount of labor.

US economic growth accelerated in 3Q amid vibrant business investment and resilient consumer spending. Economists generally expect efficiency gains to continue this year amid the AI rush.

See also: US companies slash the least jobs in three years in October

After their October meeting, Federal Reserve officials described productivity growth as “strong” even as inflation remained elevated. Chairman Kevin Warsh has said technological advances should ultimately ease price pressures, while cautioning that any AI-driven productivity payoff will gradually emerge.

Another government report out on Thursday showed initial applications for unemployment benefits declined last week to match the lowest level since 1969, highlighting a stable job market.

The productivity report showed 3Q non-farm business output, which excludes the impact of government spending, increased an annualised 3.7% — the fastest pace in a year.

See also: US Treasury borrows record US$839 bil in single week

Hours worked rose 0.1%, while hourly compensation, unadjusted for inflation, increased an annualised 2.9%. After adjusting for inflation, worker compensation rose 1.1%.

The labour share of income, the portion of output that goes to workers in the form of compensation, was 53% in 3Q of 2026, the lowest level in data back to 1947.

Separate figures out on Thursday from Challenger, Gray & Christmas showed layoff announcements were the lowest for any October in three years.

title: TOTM Technologies forms joint venture with ClaudeLabs to deliver AI consultancy, implementation and integration services
article:
TOTM Technologies, through its wholly-owned subsidiary, TOTM Labs, has entered into a strategic collaboration and joint venture agreement with ClaudeLabs on Nov 5.

Both parties will set up a Singapore-incorporated company to deliver AI consultancy, implementation and integration services to enterprise and government customers in Singapore and the region.

“It marks a further step in our strategy to build a commercial AI service business alongside its existing technology platforms,” TOTM Technologies says.

ClaudeLabs is a private company limited by shares and runs an enterprise AI consulting and implementation business. The sole director and shareholder of ClaudeLabs belongs to Freddy Lim Guo Xiong.

TOTM Technologies claims that ClaudeLabs is a “recognised community partner” in Anthropic’s ecosystem.

TOTM Technologies believes the joint venture is aligned with the group’s strategic objective of expanding its AI capabilities and deepening its participation in Singapore's rapidly developing AI ecosystem.

See also: Clearbridge Health to acquire pipes and valves business for $2.76 mil

Shares of TOTM Technologies closed unchanged at 2.1 cents on Nov 5.

title: Krispy Kreme raises revenue outlook as turnaround takes hold
article:
(Nov 5): Krispy Kreme Inc raised its revenue outlook for the year, showing that efforts to turn around the doughnut chain by refranchising and cutting costs are working.

 

The company now expects full-year net revenue to reach at least the top end of its prior range, with much of the growth coming from renewed momentum in international markets, along with online orders and its fresh delivery business in the US, chief executive officer Josh Charlesworth said in an interview.

The Charlotte, North Carolina-based donut chain now sees full-year net revenue of between US$1.35 billion and US$1.4 billion, in line with the US$1.38 billion expected by Wall Street. It had previously guided between US$1.25 billion and US$1.35 billion. Third-quarter net revenue of US$328.8 million also topped estimates.

Krispy Kreme has been working to cut costs and reduce debt for about a year to turn around its business. It cut capital expenditures for the first three quarters of the year by almost 65% from a year earlier, primarily by franchising much of its store network. It added 98 new shops around the world so far this year, nearly all of which are franchised.

During the quarter, about 42% of system-wide sales came from franchised locations, up from 25% over all of fiscal 2025. System-wide sales were up 1% in constant currency.

Krispy Kreme also aims to boost its fresh delivery business, which sells Krispy Kreme doughnuts and pastries in retailers like Walmart, Target and Publix. The company backed out of lower-performing locations about a year ago, Charlesworth said, and is focusing on locations with better traffic.

Much of the sales growth is coming from the company’s own site and app, Charlesworth said, as well as newer initiatives to sell on Walmart’s and Target’s websites.

See also: Texas blue wave erases US$130 bil from Musk stocks

Demand is largely holding up, Charlesworth said, even as many in the food and restaurant industries worry about the impacts of GLP-1s and other weight-loss drugs, as well as consumers pulling back on spending. Krispy Kreme has seen an uptick in customers ordering its “double dozens” as they look for the best value, he said.

The chain has been less affected by budget-conscious consumers pulling back since customers typically only visit two or three times per year, and are typically purchasing to share, for a holiday or for a special occasion.

title: Singapore to end most haze mitigation measures on Saturday
article:
(Nov 5): Most Singapore government agencies will cease haze mitigation measures on Saturday, as the country’s air quality improves after weeks of dense smog.

The distribution of N95 and equivalent masks through vending machines and at community clubs will end at 6pm on Nov 7, the National Environment Agency said in a statement. Air-conditioned rooms at select centres that have been designated as shelters will also close then, while haze-related measures for outdoor workers will also end on Saturday.

“The haze situation for Singapore has improved with the establishment of inter-monsoon conditions and more showers,” the agency said.

Meanwhile, the Public Health Preparedness Clinic Scheme and Haze Subsidy Scheme will be deactivated by the health ministry on Nov 12, according to the statement. The inter-agency Haze Task Force will also be stood down.

The decision comes after Singapore has enjoyed more benign readings for its pollution standards index in recent days, following weeks of “unhealthy” or “very unhealthy” air quality due to a severe wildfire season in Indonesia. The country toughened its law on cross-border haze on Wednesday, which now includes restrictions and fines for businesses dealing with entities or individuals suspected to have engaged in conduct leading to the blazes.
